CortexProbe signal flow

Prepare matched frames

  1. Build grouped masks

    Bar, wedge, or ring apertures.

    Return bar sweeps share an axis group. Prune high overlap across groups.

  2. Create synthetic responses

    Gaussian overlap × amplitude + baseline.

    Optional seeded noise.

  3. Align retained frames

    One mask, response, and group per frame.

    Check shapes and parameter bounds.

Same matched frames → independent fits

Full-data fit

Use all retained frames.

  1. Search candidates

    Compare a grid of centers and widths.

  2. Refine within bounds

    SciPy least squares refines center and width.

    At every candidate and trial geometry, solve amplitude + baseline by linear least squares.

  3. Field estimate and checks

    Center (x, y), width, amplitude, and baseline.

    In-sample R², local standard errors, and residual second-field gain.

  4. Acceptance

    Optimizer converged; R² meets the threshold; amplitude is positive; sigma is away from its bounds.

    Held-out scores do not gate acceptance.

Grouped validation

Repeat for each usable group.

  1. Hold out one group

    Keep its masks and responses separate from training.

  2. Fit the other groups

    Candidate grid → bounded refinement.

    At every candidate and trial geometry, solve amplitude + baseline by linear least squares.

  3. Freeze all five parameters

    Center (x, y), width, amplitude, and baseline stay fixed.

  4. Predict held-out frames

    Held-out masks → prediction only.

  5. Score held-out predictions

    Held-out responses → scoring only.

    Compute R² for this group.

  6. Validation summary

    Mean + sample SD of finite fold R².

    Valid / requested folds; complete / incomplete coverage.

    Complete means every requested fold has a finite R².

The full-data fit does not initialize the fold models.

Examples and recorded results are synthetic. No human-data or neural-network evaluation.
